title: No Verified Incident, No Excuse for Vietnam’s Dog-Trade Gaps
excerpt: No documented incident accompanies this report. That gap blocks honest claims about stolen pets, poison, transport, or dog farms—and demands stronger evidence before action.
body_html:
No police seizure, court verdict, intercepted shipment, or emergency warning appears here. That absence does not prove safety. It means claims about cyanide bait, stolen family dogs, secret transport, or uninspected meat cannot be presented as fact without named sources, dates, locations, and official records.

Myths need records, not repetition

“Farm-raised dogs” cannot be accepted or rejected through slogans. Establishing supply-chain conditions requires traceable ownership records, veterinary documentation, transport permits, quarantine compliance, slaughter inspection, and enforcement data. No such Vietnamese records accompany this report. No verified basis supports the claim that all dogs in trade come from farms—or that all come from stolen homes.

Public health demands exact language

Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters wounds, broken skin, or mucous membranes through bites or scratches. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. After possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical care. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. WHO guidance supports these medical facts.

Demand evidence. Demand protection.

Vietnamese families deserve transparent enforcement against animal theft, illegal transport, unsafe slaughter, and disease exposure where authorities document those violations. SDE’s campaign demand goes further: complete abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition and add your name to that public demand.
